npp-plugins.description:
Dockable multi-pattern search and color-coded display for log files and large documents.

Features:
- Define a list of search patterns, each with its own foreground/background color
- Search types: normal, escaped, regular expression, multiline regex; case and whole-word options
- Per-pattern group, order#, comment, hide-text and line/word selection
- Dockable result window (Scintilla) with per-pattern coloring and double-click jump to the source line
- Matched lines marked with a green bar in the editor's change-history margin
- Result-window filter, zoom, context menu, and RTF/text export
- Bidirectional scroll sync between the result window and the editor
- Save/Load pattern sets as AnalyseDoc XML (wire-compatible with the Windows plugin); auto-persisted across launches
- Options dialog and Help/About

npp-plugins.description:
Work with text and data arranged in columns. Elastic tabstops keep columns aligned as you type; column alignment (left, right, numeric, or a custom delimiter/regex); sort by column (binary, locale, or numeric; ascending or descending; custom keys).

Search and replace within a rectangular or multiple-selection region (Normal, Extended, or Regex), with per-match regex-calculate substitutions and configurable region indicators.

Calculate: evaluate a per-row expression (with cross-row references) and insert the result as a new column.

Timestamps: convert between counters (Unix, Windows FILETIME, Excel 1900/1904) and date/time text, locale- and time-zone-aware. Also Add/Average numbers, tabs to/from separated-values conversion, and rectangular-selection tools.

Regex uses ICU syntax (named groups, look-behind, \p{...} classes) and is Unicode-correct; time-zone data comes from the OS (/usr/share/zoneinfo).

Builds for arm64 and x86_64.

npp-plugins.description:
Display Notepad++'s line numbers in a custom format, shown in an extra editor margin: hexadecimal, relative (Vim-style distance from the caret line), or decimal with a custom start — plus a configurable starting number and optional margin text colour / background / bold. The active mode is check-marked and persists between sessions.

Because the host owns the built-in line-number margin, the plugin renders in its own extra margin next to it; hide the host's line numbers in Preferences to see only the custom format.

Builds for arm64 and x86_64.

Note: no default shortcuts on Linux - assign your own in Settings > Shortcut Mapper > Plugin commands.

npp-plugins.description:
Doxygen comment generator for Notepad++. Put your cursor on the blank line above a function, press Ctrl+Alt+Shift+D, and NppDoxy inserts a /** ... */ block with @brief, one @param line per argument, @return, and @details — each pre-filled with $(...) jump markers. Tab cycles through the markers; Escape clears them.

Features:
- Comment Function — parse the function signature below the cursor and generate a fully-populated doc block
- Comment File — insert a file-header block with @file + @brief
- Active Commenting — type /** above a function and press Enter, and NppDoxy auto-runs Comment Function
- Jump locations — Tab through $(placeholder) markers in the generated block; Escape clears them
- Language-specific doc_start/doc_line/doc_end delimiters

Supported languages: C, C++, Java, Python, PHP, JavaScript, C#.

Port Author: Andrew Letov

npp-plugins.description:
Remove or replace "gremlin" characters — invisible, control, or non-ASCII characters that sneak into files and cause subtle bugs (BBEdit-style "Zap Gremlins").

Search categories:
- Non-ASCII characters (above U+007F)
- Control characters (C0 except Tab/CR/LF, plus DEL)
- Null (ASCII 0) characters

Actions:
- Delete
- Replace with a character of your choice
- Replace with a \uXXXX code, optionally transliterating common typographic characters to ASCII first (smart quotes, dashes, NBSP, ...)
- Replace with an HTML entity (named where available, else numeric)

Operates on the selection if any, else the whole document, as one undo step. Includes an optional "Highlight gremlins" toggle.

The formatting engine is a faithful C++ reimplementation of the original .NET library, validated byte-for-byte against the upstream Windows test corpus.
